answer.rationale: P99 latency spike to 5x target correlates precisely with the release 2 hours ago. Memory b1 demonstrates that rollback cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact and the prior build was stable. Memory b6 shows staged release gating and canary cohorts can catch regressions—suggesting this one may not have been caught in those gates, making it a strong rollback candidate. With settlement traffic at peak and writes heavy, the release is the highest-probability root cause. Rollback is the fastest way to restore the write path to known-good behavior, preserves all in-flight transactions, and recovers availability within minutes. This is lower risk than capacity adds (which won't address a code regression) or circuit breakers (which would degrade rather than restore service). The timing correlation is strong enough to justify the one available intervention slot.
